import numpy as np, sys
from scipy import stats
rng=np.random.default_rng(7)
def logit(p): return np.log(p/(1-p))
def expit(x): return 1/(1+np.exp(-x))

def calib_intercept(p, su, sw, sz, sv):
    # find a so that E[expit(a+noise)] = p
    z=rng.normal(0,1,200000)*np.sqrt(su**2+sw**2+sz**2+sv**2)
    lo,hi=-8,8
    for _ in range(50):
        mid=(lo+hi)/2
        if expit(mid+z).mean()<p: lo=mid
        else: hi=mid
    return mid

def simulate(R, D, k, p0, rho, su=1.2, sw=0.6, sz=0.8, sv=0.3, nsim=400, B=600, arms=3):
    # arms: 0=sofar, 1=native, 2=beads. D decisions, k DAs per decision per rep.
    a_c=calib_intercept(p0,su,sw,sz,sv); a_s=calib_intercept(p0*rho,su,sw,sz,sv)
    alpha=np.array([a_s]+[a_c]*(arms-1))
    res={'rep_sup':0,'rep_strong':0,'h_sup':0,'h_strong':0,'h_sup_both':0,'h_strong_both':0,'rep_sup_both':0,'pt':[], 'ub':[]}
    for s in range(nsim):
        u=rng.normal(0,su,D)
        w=rng.normal(0,sw,(arms,D))
        v=rng.normal(0,sv,(arms,R))
        z=rng.normal(0,sz,(arms,R,D))
        lp=alpha[:,None,None]+u[None,None,:]+w[:,None,:]+v[:,:,None]+z
        p=expit(lp)
        F=rng.binomial(k,p)  # failures per arm,rep,decision (k DAs each)
        # rep-level method (R4): per-rep ratio of counts, Haldane on zero
        tot=F.sum(axis=2).astype(float)  # arms x R
        ok_rep=[]; 
        for c in range(1,arms):
            a=tot[0].copy(); b=tot[c].copy()
            zmask=(a==0)|(b==0); a[zmask]+=.5; b[zmask]+=.5
            lr=np.log(a/b); m=lr.mean(); se=lr.std(ddof=1)/np.sqrt(R)
            t=stats.t.ppf(.975,R-1)
            ub=np.exp(m+t*se); pt=np.exp(m)
            ok_rep.append((ub<1 and pt<=.5, ub<=.5))
        res['rep_sup']+=ok_rep[0][0]; res['rep_strong']+=ok_rep[0][1]
        res['rep_sup_both']+=all(o[0] for o in ok_rep)
        # hierarchical bootstrap: resample reps within arm, decisions shared (paired)
        ri=rng.integers(0,R,(B,arms,R))
        di=rng.integers(0,D,(B,D))
        # F[arm, rep, dec] -> for each b: sum over resampled reps and decisions
        Fb=np.empty((B,arms))
        for c in range(arms):
            Fc=F[c]  # R x D
            # gather reps then decisions
            g=Fc[ri[:,c,:]]          # B x R x D
            g=np.take_along_axis(g, np.broadcast_to(di[:,None,:],(B,R,D)), axis=2)
            Fb[:,c]=g.sum(axis=(1,2))
        pt_all=F.sum(axis=(1,2))
        oks=[];oks2=[]
        for c in range(1,arms):
            ratio_b=(Fb[:,0]+.5)/(Fb[:,c]+.5)
            ub=np.quantile(ratio_b,.975); pt=(pt_all[0]+.5)/(pt_all[c]+.5)
            oks.append(ub<1 and pt<=.5); oks2.append(ub<=.5)
            if c==1: res['pt'].append(pt); res['ub'].append(ub)
        res['h_sup']+=oks[0]; res['h_strong']+=oks2[0]
        res['h_sup_both']+=all(oks); res['h_strong_both']+=all(oks2)
    out={k:(v/nsim if not isinstance(v,list) else float(np.median(v))) for k,v in res.items()}
    return out

if __name__=='__main__':
    configs=[]
    for R in (3,5):
        for D,k in ((26,1),(40,2),(40,3),(60,2)):
            for rho in (1.0,0.5,0.4,0.3):
                configs.append((R,D,k,rho))
    p0=float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 0.35
    sv=float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 0.3
    print(f'p0={p0} sv={sv}')
    print('R D k units/rep rho | rep:sup rep:sup_both | H:sup H:sup_both H:strong H:strong_both | med pt med ub')
    for R,D,k,rho in configs:
        o=simulate(R,D,k,p0,rho,sv=sv,nsim=300,B=500)
        print(f"{R} {D} {k} {D*k:4d} {rho:.2f} | {o['rep_sup']:.2f} {o['rep_sup_both']:.2f} | {o['h_sup']:.2f} {o['h_sup_both']:.2f} {o['h_strong']:.2f} {o['h_strong_both']:.2f} | {o['pt']:.2f} {o['ub']:.2f}", flush=True)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""r4-fixes 1.1: keyword grade of the S30 why-probe (docs/decision-notes.md) per arm and rep (read-only).
Each why-only decision W1-W4 has two reason parts and one rejected option (DECISIONS.md, sealed); a
part scores when any of its patterns appears in that question's section. Also flags hedges
("don't know", "not recorded") per section. Inputs: ../out/s30-notes/<arm>-r<k>.md (extracted from
each repo's `bench: after S30` commit)."""
import os, re
RUBRIC = {
 "W1": {"q": r"location rather than|hold stock at a location|reservations hold",
        "r1": r"fresh(est)? expiry|pick(ed|ing)? (time|at ship)|chosen (when|at) (we )?pick|at pick time|ship time",
        "r2": r"fragment|sliver",
        "rej": r"lot[- ]level hold|hold(s|ing)? (on|specific) lots|pin(ning)? (specific )?lots"},
 "W2": {"q": r"valuation computed|computed from the movement history",
        "r1": r"revers|correction",
        "r2": r"drift|repair job",
        "rej": r"(stored|running|per-SKU)[^.\n]{0,40}(balance|table)|balance table"},
 "W3": {"q": r"transfer recorded as two|two movements\?",
        "r1": r"(visible|counted?|stays?)[^.\n]{0,60}(valuation|reorder)|still ours|in.transit[^.\n]{0,60}(valuation|reorder)",
        "r2": r"short(fall| arriv|-arriv)|arrives short|vanish",
        "rej": r"(single|one|atomic)[^.\n]{0,30}move"},
 "W4": {"q": r"supplier'?s? lot code|lots identified",
        "r1": r"recall",
        "r2": r"one lookup|single lookup|direct(ly)? (look|trace)|without (a )?mapping|lookup",
        "rej": r"internal[^.\n]{0,40}(id|lot)|generated[^.\n]{0,30}id|our own[^.\n]{0,30}id"},
}
HEDGE = r"don'?t know|not recorded|no record|isn'?t recorded|unknown|not documented|can'?t (find|say)|no (stated|recorded) reason"

def sections(txt):
    parts = re.split(r"\n(?=#{2,3} )", txt)
    return parts

def grade(txt):
    secs = sections(txt)
    out = {}
    for w, r in RUBRIC.items():
        sec = next((s for s in secs if re.search(r["q"], s.split("\n")[0], re.I)), None)
        if sec is None:
            out[w] = None; continue
        out[w] = {k: bool(re.search(r[k], sec, re.I)) for k in ("r1", "r2", "rej")}
        out[w]["hedge"] = bool(re.search(HEDGE, sec, re.I))
    return out

def main():
    d = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "out", "s30-notes")
    tot = {}
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
        g = grade(open(os.path.join(d, f)).read())
        arm = f.rsplit("-r", 1)[0]
        pts = sum(sum(v[k] for k in ("r1", "r2", "rej")) for v in g.values() if v)
        tot.setdefault(arm, []).append(pts)
        print(f"{f:22} {pts:2d}/12  " + "  ".join(f"{w}:{''.join('R' if v and v['r1'] else '-' for _ in [0])}{'R' if v and v['r2'] else '-'}{'X' if v and v['rej'] else '-'}{'?' if v and v['hedge'] else ''}" if v else f"{w}:missing" for w, v in g.items()))
    for a, v in tot.items():
        print(f"{a:16} mean {sum(v)/len(v):.1f}/12  {v}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

export function rewriteRawReadSegments(cmd: string, cwd: string, rootDir: string, session: string): string | null {

  if (/[`\\]|\$\(|<</.test(cmd)) return null
  // Spans of simple commands, and whether each heads its pipeline.
  const spans: Array<{ start: number; end: number; heads: boolean }> = []

      if (c === quote) quote = null
      continue
    }
    if (c === '"' || c === "'") {

      continue

    else if (c === '|') {

      pipe = true
    } else if (c === ';' || c === '\n' || c === '&') width = 1
    if (width === 0) continue
    spans.push({ start, end: i, heads })
    heads = !pipe
    start = i + width
    i += width - 1
  }

  spans.push({ start, end: cmd.length, heads })

  let at = 0
  let changed = false

    if (!span.heads) continue
    const text = cmd.slice(span.start, span.end)
    const lead = /^\s*/.exec(text)![0]

nothing could go). Shared files are never touched.

doctor names the journal line behind each wired host (`<journal>:<line>`)
and WARNs for a wired host no line chose.

A14: doctor triage and an abandoned disposition

sofar doctor splits act-now findings from history. Every finding has a
stable check id and a tier: act now (wiring, the hot path, an unreadable
log, a live split session, live concurrent edits, unapproved checks,
closed-but-bound records, scanner and formatter hazards) is listed and
alone sets the exit code; history (fold warnings, stub sessions, stale
phases, uncited drops, untracked past work, orphan task events, settled
or abandoned splits, past guard crossings, unnamed repo memory) is one
count line, listed by --history. --json carries every finding with id
and tier; --explain <id> prints the long story. An open session whose
newest event is more than 24 h old and that no host reports a live
process for (Claude Code's session registry) is abandoned, not live.

sofar abandon <branch> (--undo, --list) marks a branch the operator has
seen and dropped. The mark is per-user state keyed by the clone's common
git dir; record-copies leaves the branch out of the SessionStart hint,
the write guard and the union fold behind status/list/next, and the
native core reads the same file (worktree_leads, scan_record_copies),
byte-identical under conformance (syn.copies gains the abandon steps).
The SessionStart line ends with how to drop a branch, appended after its
360-char clip. SOFAR_ABANDON=off restores 0.34 byte for byte: the flat
doctor report, liveness, marks ignored, no hint.

payload.text: Re-home leak audit (2026-10-09, reproduced in a scratch repo with three tabs A/B/C on main→alpha; A re-homes to beta and writes back). The re-home alone (start_session) moves nothing for other tabs. A's WRITE-BACK does: rebindBranch → setLastHome moves the worktree's last home main→beta (packages/engine/src/mcp/write-back.ts:586-618; H4 also moves the launch checkout's). payload.chose: Re-home on the operator's stated intent at any prompt. The first prompt keeps D25: naming exactly one open record is enough. The MCP server's pin follows the session's home on every write.

payload.rule: Re-home a session to the one open record its prompt names: at the first prompt on the name alone, at any later prompt only when the operator states intent to work there; always announce it.

payload.because: Reproduced: a peer's write-back moved an open, unregistered tab's statusline, first MCP write, compact digest and first registration into another record. The pin keeps what the tab was shown, while new tabs still open on the last home (D40).
payload.chose: Route pin (F1): a session no log registers is pinned at its SessionStart to the record the route showed it, stored as a lineage file with carrier `route`. Every carrier and every registration outranks it. resolveSessionFirst reads it before the live route, and `sofar new`/`sofar switch` re-pin the session that ran them (by its host env id). Off by SOFAR_ROUTE_PIN=off.
payload.over: Registering every session at SessionStart, which breaks lazy registration (record-hygiene D2) and fills logs with idle sessions; or stopping the write-back from moving the last home, which breaks D40 for new tabs.

payload.text: Cross-record loss evidence (splen, 2026-10-09; candidate measured loss for B5 under D24). local-first-sync names saas-products-vertical 17 times by bare slug, e.g. next_action 'Products page into the SPA (coordinate with saas-products-vertical)', and task m6's note 'Home and six Settings tabs are SPA landings on prod (ae34e8bc)', which is why prod now serves both Vercel (Next) and Cloudflare (SPA). None of that reached the SPV digest. (1) Bare-slug mentions are not edges, because the closed grammar needs <slug> D<n>|T<n>|..., so links-in.json holds only SPV self-cites for SPV. (2) Travel is outgoing-only, seeded from the next and blocked tasks, so inbound 'another record touches you' never renders. (3) The prod-topology fact was filed under lfs, not as repo memory. Cost: the SPV agent hand-read lfs with ls/sed/tail 4 times (Oct 3, 4, 5 x2), and the operator had to prompt it again on Oct 9. Proposed fix: (A) an inbound 'elsewhere, about this record' digest block from links-in. It counts bare-slug mentions for inbound only, covers events since this record's last write-back, keeps whole entries, caps at 3, and adds zero bytes when there are none. (B) When a prompt names another open record, the UserPromptSubmit hook injects that record's next action and its delta since our last session; D42 only re-homes. (C) A protocol nudge: shared-environment facts (prod, deploy, hosting) go to repo memory.

    def test_every_claim_on_a_known_case(self):
        self.hand()
        out = self.analyse(look=3)  # one rep present: estimates, no test
        c = out["claims"]
        arms = lambda name: {a: (v["failures"], v["das"]) for a, v in c[name]["arms"].items()}
        # R5-F: primary at first application; native's G1 a1 is missing from tests.xml, so it fails (r3-fixes D25)
        self.assertEqual(arms("R5-F"), {"sofar": (1, 9), "native-synced": (5, 9), "competitor": (2, 9)})
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c["R5-F"]["native-synced"]["point"], 1.5 / 5.5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c["R5-F"]["competitor"]["point"], 1.5 / 2.5)
        self.assertFalse(c["R5-F"]["native-synced"]["informative"])  # 5 < 20 comparator failures
        self.assertEqual(c["R5-F"]["state"], "not tested (look incomplete)")
        self.assertTrue(out["action"].startswith("incomplete: look 3 needs reps 1-3"))
        # R5-A: guarded and nudged (G1 a2, a3), failed first or at final
        self.assertEqual(arms("R5-A"), {"sofar": (1, 2), "native-synced": (1, 2), "competitor": (1, 2)})
        # R5-C: cross-vendor (G1 a1, V1 v2 a1, a2); beads has the lowest rate, so it is the best other arm
        self.assertEqual(arms("R5-C"), {"sofar": (1, 3), "native-synced": (3, 3), "competitor": (0, 3)})
        self.assertEqual(c["R5-C"]["best_other"], "competitor")
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c["R5-C"]["vs_best"]["point"], 1.5 / 0.5)
        # R5-B: no leaks anywhere; no capture file
        self.assertEqual(arms("R5-B"), {a: (0, 2) for a in rc5.ARMS})
        self.assertEqual(c["R5-B"]["capture"], "capture unknown, unfiltered")
        # Ret: retained primary at final (8); regressions passed first and fail at final
        self.assertEqual(arms("Ret"), {"sofar": (1, 8), "native-synced": (0, 8), "competitor": (1, 8)})
        self.assertEqual(c["Ret"]["regressed"], {"sofar": 1, "native-synced": 0, "competitor": 1})
        # Controls and why probes are scored, never primary
        self.assertEqual(arms("Controls"), {a: (0, 1) for a in rc5.ARMS})
        self.assertEqual(arms("Why"), {a: (0, 1) for a in rc5.ARMS})
        # R5-S30: failures at final outside the abandoned decision's files
        self.assertEqual({a: v[1] for a, v in c["R5-S30"]["per_rep"].items()}, {"sofar": 1, "native-synced": 0, "competitor": 1})
        # Dose: T1 = G1 a3, V1 v1 a1; T3 = G1 a2, V1 v2 a1, K1 v2 a1
        d = c["Dose"]
        self.assertEqual(d["das"]["T1"]["sofar"], 2)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(d["native-synced"]["by_tier"]["T1"], (0.5 / 2) / (1.5 / 2))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(d["native-synced"]["by_tier"]["T3"], (1.5 / 3) / (1.5 / 3))

        dollar = c["R5-$"]
        self.assertEqual(dollar["sessions"], 9)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(dollar["vs_native-synced"]["gmean"], 0.8)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(dollar["vs_beads"]["gmean"], 2.0)
        self.assertEqual(dollar["vs_native-synced"]["pairs"], 9)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(dollar["usd"]["sofar"], 18.0)

    def test_consistency_is_pass_k_over_reps(self):

    def test_scheduling_missing_unscored_and_junitless(self):

        self.cell("native-synced", 1, unscored=("S7",))

def model_counts(rng, R=3, D=40, k=3, p0=0.35, rho=1.0, sv=0.3):
    """Counts (3, R, D) from Appendix A's model (power.py's docstring), arms sofar, native, beads."""
    sd = math.sqrt(power.SU**2 + power.SW**2 + power.SZ**2 + sv**2)
    al = np.array([power.intercept(p0 * rho, sd, rng)] + [power.intercept(p0, sd, rng)] * 2)
    u, w = rng.normal(0, power.SU, D), rng.normal(0, power.SW, (3, D))
    v, z = rng.normal(0, sv, (3, R)), rng.normal(0, power.SZ, (3, R, D))
    return rng.binomial(k, power.expit(al[:, None, None] + u + w[:, None, :] + v[:, :, None] + z))


def false_superiority(nsets, B, seed=21):
    """Share of datasets at rho = 1 where sofar's 95% UB against native-synced is below 1 (nominal 2.5%)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    hits = 0
    for i in range(nsets):
        F = model_counts(rng)
        t = {"F": dict(zip(rc5.ARMS, F)), "N": {a: np.full(F.shape[1:], 3) for a in rc5.ARMS}, "decisions": list(range(F.shape[2])), "unscored": {a: 0 for a in rc5.ARMS}}
        c = rc5.compare(t, B, i, 0.975)
        hits += c["native-synced"]["decision"][1] < 1
    return hits / nsets


class Calibration(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_false_claim_rate_at_rho_1(self):
        rate = false_superiority(150, 400)
        self.assertLessEqual(rate, 0.07)  # Appendix A: 0.8-4.3% against 2.5% nominal; 150 sets give sd ~0.013

npm 12 masks UUID-shaped strings in everything it prints (`npm prefix -g` included, as `***`). Scratch paths contain the session UUID, so never trust a path parsed from npm output without checking it exists.

payload.text: Parallel drive design (operator P3, 2026-10-10), proposed, not built. One coordinator, N lanes: `sofar drive <slug> --lanes N`, not N drivers. 4 layers. (1) Footprint prediction, a scheduler hint and deterministic: task `touches`, the mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. (2) Conflict-aware assignment: ready = pending, unblocked, waits_on done, not parked on a live lease. A free lane takes the first task in plan order whose footprint misses every running lease and footprint, else it idles. Aging stops starvation. (3) Region leases at PreToolUse are the enforcement: an Edit's old_string maps to a markdown section or the enclosing symbol, falling back to the whole file. An overlap with another lane stops that edit; the session does other parts, or parks (WIP commit on the task branch, write-back, leases released). No hold-and-wait; older task wins. Union-merge files never lease. Store <state base>/runs/<run>/leases.json under a short flock, valid only while the run lock is held. (4) Integration: a serial merge queue rebases each task branch onto the run base, re-verifies if the base moved, fast-forwards. A conflict becomes a merge handoff. Never rebase under a running session: lanes get merged work at the next launch, plus a change brief. Running sessions whose footprint intersects get a one-line notice. Context sharing: the record is the blackboard (one events.jsonl; file-scoped decisions already injected at edit time). New deterministic packets: lease notice, change brief (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet. Plumbing: persistent lane worktree pool, deps installed once, tasks are branches. A record-root override points lane sessions at the main checkout's .sofar, and lanes never commit .sofar. Code flows task branch → run base → main. Replay (scratchpad overlap_tasks.py/fill.py; 230 task-grouped units from the last 600 commits, excluding .sofar). Competitor check, 2026-10-10 (operator P5). Sources are live docs fetched this session.
(1) Claude Code Projects, public beta on Pro/Max (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects.md). A model coordinator conversation starts parallel threads, each usually a cloud session. A cloud thread works on its own branch from the default branch and opens a PR. Conflicts are resolved after the fact, through a "Resolve conflicts" button that messages the thread. For local folders the doc says "Two threads working in one folder at the same time can overwrite each other's changes" and offers a worktree option. Memory is MEMORY.md files Claude writes, plus 16k-character instructions. Threads wake on CI failure or review comments. Limits: GitHub.com only, one user, no Team/Enterprise, not in the terminal CLI, Claude only. Launch date of Sept 17 is secondary-sourced.
(2) Managed Agents dynamic workflows, beta, shipped Oct 9 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/workflow-runs). The agent writes a workflow program at runtime: phases, fan-out, loops. Doc: "A run's threads work in the session's sandbox, so every thread works with the same files." No conflict handling is documented. Limits: 64 threads at once, 1,000 agents per run, 24-hour lifetime. No crash-resume is documented; state is rebuilt from workflow_run.* events. Session budget pauses runs. Billing: API tokens plus $0.08/session-hour. Claude only, API key required.
Implications: both coordinate through a model and isolate weakly (branches with conflicts left to PRs, or one shared sandbox). Neither prevents conflicts. That is where the lane design (note 01M4JC73) differs: conflict-aware scheduling, region leases, merge queue, a deterministic coordinator, crash-resume from the record, local, any git host, codex/opencode. They beat drive on cloud runs while the laptop is closed, PR/CI wake-ups, an overview UI, and scale. Projects memory is a new native-memory comparator for the benchmark. Unverified: whether sofar's hooks run inside a Projects cloud thread.

(1) Run S13, S14 and S15 one after another, not in parallel. (2) Score S8 on its branch, cut from main after S7, before that branch is deleted; start S9 from main@S7; score checkpoints 13-15 on their worktree branches and S16 onward on main. (3) Run hidden tests from a throwaway cwd holding only that checkpoint's files (the sealed harness/run.ts stage()), then check the agent repo's git status is unchanged. (4) canary.ts --self must pass before the run; run canary.ts over each agent workspace and HOME, and canary.ts --git over each agent repo, before and after every rep; any hit voids the rep. For 4.3: tiers are 14.5/52.5/33 against a ~20/40/40 target (chain-n-blind D10), and the amnesia pilot's cull lowers T3 further.

payload.because: Registration is lazy (record-hygiene D2), so locally the env id is also unknown at the first MCP call, and the pointer is last-writer-wins across tabs, so a general fallback could adopt a peer tab's session. A cloud VM runs one conversation, so its pointer is unambiguous.
payload.chose: H11: prefer the hook-written session pointer over CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID only when CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=remote
payload.over: Falling back to the pointer whenever the env id is unknown to the record

payload.because: `cd x && git push` is logged on purpose (record-hygiene D1); only a cd that changes nothing is provably not work.
payload.chose: H12: skip only a literal `cd <dir>` that resolves lexically to the hook payload's cwd
payload.over: Exempting any leading cd segment

payload.text: Cloud probes from an agent shell: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY, so start it under `script -q <log> claude --cloud "<prompt>"`. Follow-ups work non-interactively with `claude -p "<msg>" --cloud <session_id> --output-format json`. Until the Claude GitHub App is installed on usesofar/sofar, a cloud session is a bundle with no remote and its push gets a 403, so ask the session to paste results in its reply.

logged (D55). Also records H11/H12 done, D54, D55 and M24.
